audit_findings.title: Post-merger shares are paired with pre-merger owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 75.034657 million merger shares issued; valuation denominator 208.462933 million versus 127.2 million shares outstanding at December 28, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: The merger-expanded share denominator reduces per-share value while the OE numerator excludes American Woodmark operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, at the effective time of the Merger (the “Effective Time”), each equity interest of American Woodmark issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will be automatically converted into the right to receive a number of shares of the Company’s common stock equal to 5.15 shares, which collectively will represent approximately 37 percent of the fully diluted shares outstanding of the combined company immediately prior to the execution and delivery of the Merger Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possibility. The valuation combines post-closing shares and balance-sheet items with $80.4 million of pre-closing MasterBrand owner earnings. The omitted target earnings make the reported per-share values conservative, but the numerator and denominator do not represent the same equity claim, so none of the scenario values is decision-ready.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios using post-closing combined owner earnings, shares, cash and liabilities; alternatively revert every input to the pre-closing MasterBrand perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Incremental acquisition financing cost is absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $375.0 million Term Loan A drawn, including $367.5 million used to settle American Woodmark debt
audit_findings.mechanism: Because debt principal is not deducted in an equity-level OE model, sustainable interest, financing-fee amortization and related cash burdens must reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company amended its 2024 Credit Agreement on November 3, 2025 to obtain $ 375.0 million of delayed draw term loan commitments that will be used to repay and terminate American Woodmark’s existing indebtedness, the funding of which is dependent on the closing of the Merger.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing post-closing financing burden is demonstrated: FY2025 OE predates the loan, while the latest quarter contains only about one month of its interest. The exact annual cost cannot be established without the applicable SOFR margin and sustainable debt schedule, but a $375.0 million variable-rate loan is reasonably capable of materially changing an $80.4 million OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Calculate the post-closing annual interest and fee run rate using actual loan pricing, average balances, required amortization and cash sweeps, then rerun OE and every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $241.6 million, or $1.16 per valuation share and 18.4% of the $1,310.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for working capital, capital expenditure, integration or transaction commitments must be retained in operations rather than added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe that our cash and cash equivalent balances, along with available cash from operating cash flows and credit facilities, will be adequate to fund our typical needs, including working capital requirements and projected capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds all $241.6 million, but the filings do not quantify minimum operating cash. No restricted cash is separately reported at June 28, 2026, yet unrestricted cash is not necessarily surplus. If none were excess, base value would fall mechanically from $6.29 to about $5.13 per share; the record cannot establish how much of that maximum adjustment is warranted.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a post-closing liquidity schedule covering seasonal working capital, minimum cash, committed capital spending, integration payments and transaction obligations, then add only the residual demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Deal costs may materially depress the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.9 million of FY2025 acquisition-related costs versus the $80.4 million OE anchor; a further $44.0 million was filed for the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained nonrecurring transaction costs depress normalized OE, while adding back costs that recur under an acquisition-led strategy would overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company incurred $ 28.9 million and $ 25.4 million of acquisition-related costs for the years ended December 28, 2025 and December 29, 2024 , respectively, which are recorded within selling, general and administrative expenses in the consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The costs are filed and large relative to the anchor, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE reconciliation retained, excluded or partly normalized them. Continued acquisition costs in 2026 also prevent treating the entire FY2025 amount as automatically nonrecurring. Materiality therefore depends on classification that remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace each acquisition-related cost through the OE reconciliation and separate transaction execution, integration, severance, stock compensation and recurring acquisition-platform spending; rerun only for supportable normalization adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Customer-relationship amortization may represent economic depletion
audit_findings.magnitude: $25.6 million of FY2025 amortization, equal to 31.8% of the $80.4 million OE anchor; $25.6 million annually was forecast for 2026-2030 before the American Woodmark acquisition
audit_findings.mechanism: A full amortization add-back raises OE unless maintenance reinvestment captures the economic cost of customer attrition and relationship replacement.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortizable intangible assets, principally customer relationships, are subject to amortization on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful life, ranging from 16 to 20 years, based on the assessment of a number of factors that may impact useful life, including customer attrition rates and other relevant factors.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that customer relationships have finite 16-to-20-year lives and that amortization is substantial. It does not establish whether amortization was fully added back or whether advertising, selling investment or acquisitions already capture the replacement cost. The possible overstatement is therefore significant in scale but unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE reconciliation, quantify the portion of amortization added back, and estimate recurring relationship-replacement spending from customer attrition, sales investment and acquisition history before rerunning OE.

audit_findings.title: Uncapped separation indemnities are omitted contingent senior claims
audit_findings.mechanism: A crystallized indemnity would reduce cash or create a senior liability ahead of common equity, affecting the bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Indemnities that we may be required to provide Fortune Brands are not subject to any cap, may be significant and could negatively impact our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The uncapped contractual exposure is documented, but no filed claim amount, probability or estimable loss is supplied. Consequently, it cannot be dismissed as immaterial, yet the record also cannot establish a valuation adjustment. The general disclosure that ordinary litigation is not expected to be material does not quantify these specific indemnities.
audit_findings.action: Review the separation, tax-allocation and employee-matters agreements; obtain a schedule of notices, asserted claims, limitation periods, insurance and post-FY2025 developments; adjust the bridge only for a filed or supportably estimated exposure.
